significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish the form-(iii) law that detection AUC "falls in tandem with transmission strength" as a reference model diverges from the shared base, alongside the causal-mechanistic claim that transmission and detectability depend on the same initialization-specific geometry. This would establish both a phenomenon—same-base references detect otherwise neutral trait payloads while different-base references approach chance—and a mechanism that fixes expectations for detectors at intermediate divergence, rather than merely showing that some trait representation exists. Verified false and verified true are distinguishable: failure of same-base detection or of the coupled degradation would rule out the proposed detection–transmission symmetry, although it would not rule out every shared-initialization explanation of subliminal learning. Cloud et al.'s "Subliminal Learning: Language models transmit behavioral traits via hidden signals in data" makes shared initialization and failed human/generic-judge detection load-bearing observations; after topic substitution, those generic facts alone would merit only the topic median, while the claim-specific coupled degradation law supports the higher score.

reach.justification: The named handle is a "practical auditor built from a same-base reference model," instantiated as either "gradient alignment" or "a probe on the reference's activations" and intended to flag and identify hidden traits in candidate corpora. It is ex ante because it audits "distillation and synthetic-data pipelines" before those corpora are used for training, giving practitioners an opportunity to reject or gate data rather than merely explain a completed failure. After re-extraction on another model, the claim predicts a transferable relation—detection performance should degrade with reference divergence in tandem with transmission strength—but its asserted scope is constrained by access to the teacher's base or a close approximation and may not cover unknown-provenance data. The downstream users therefore include pipeline auditors and model deployers, not only subliminal-learning researchers; topic substitution would remove this auditor, its lead time, and the divergence relation, so the topic alone would not retain this score.
